svg.text: Fog-Resilient Smart Road Lane Illumination — Wiring Diagram
Arduino UNO · DHT11 · LDR · laser + phototransistor · 74HC595 with 8 guiding LEDs · LCD 16×2 (I2C) · 2 buttons · status LED
switches the laser on and off for every reading
laser beam → fog chamber (30–50 cm) → phototransistor
ready-made module: series resistor is built in
bare diode: add ≈ 100 Ω in series
both wired to ground with INPUT_PULLUP — no external resistor
Status LED — fog / fault / not calibrated
GUIDING LIGHT — eight LEDs on a shift register
≈ 6 mA per LED · chip max 70 mA
LEDs on/off only, no PWM dimming
contrast: small trimmer on the backpack
PHYSICAL PLACEMENT — three LEDs travel along the lane, slower in dense fog
lane model inside the fog chamber
• Everything runs from the USB 5 V rail — about 165 mA in total.
• 74HC595: VCC and MR to 5 V, GND to ground, 100 nF across the supply pins,
and OE (pin 13) straight to ground. Data, latch and clock are plain D11–D13.
• Each LED draws ≈ 6 mA (470 Ω); one 595 carries 70 mA in total. For brighter
road LEDs use a TPIC6B595 or add ULN2803 drivers.
• LCD: I2C backpack — SDA to A4, SCL to A5, VCC 5 V, GND. Blank screen: turn the trimmer.
• The laser is switched by Q1, never straight from a pin. Keep the phototransistor
in a black tube, aligned with the beam, 30–50 cm away.
• D6–D10, A3 and D0/D1 (USB serial, AI data recording) stay free.
• Every ground symbol is the same net — join all grounds on the breadboard.
